PullRequest.Title: sessions: Fix connection diagnostics focus and lifecycle
PullRequest.Body:
Address review follow-ups from #336214: contain keyboard focus while copying, release sheets when their auxiliary window closes, and discard accessible snapshots when their provider is disposed.

Add regression coverage for pending actions, window teardown, and accessible provider replacement.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Closing or unregistering an auxiliary window bypassed the sheet's sole close path, leaving the sheet DisposableStore, rendered DOM/body state, caller closures, and unresolved promise reachable for the remaining workbench lifetime.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Auxiliary-window sheet teardown retained DOM nodes, listeners, body resources, and pending async continuations after the owning window closed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added filtered one-shot window lifecycle listener invokes onDismiss for the sheet's owning window, and close now removes the overlay synchronously while that window is closing, disposing listeners/body resources and resolving the pending sheet interaction instead of retaining them.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, buildMobileSheetShell registered all sheet DOM/window/viewport listeners in a DisposableStore but had no auxiliary-window teardown subscription; the only cleanup path was shell.close(), and callers such as showMobileContentSheet awaited a promise resolved only from close's animation callback. The added regression tests exercise unregister and beforeunload and require the auxiliary dialog/listeners to be released and the pending promise to resolve. blame attributes the base shell lifecycle to a51c7371fac13bbf9413c94ef7a2c6d6711de695.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, keyboard-navigate, and dismiss a mobile picker/content sheet in a live window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sheet construction synchronously creates the overlay and controls and registers DOM, visualViewport, and two global window-lifecycle listeners. Each Tab keydown rebuilds one focus-target array; normal dismissal disposes all listeners immediately, then waits 180 ms for the close animation before removing the overlay and resolving the caller promise.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Focus-trap work scales with the number of header and body focus targets in the one open sheet. The diff removes the per-target aria-disabled filter, so changed Tab handling performs fewer attribute reads than before. Listener state scales with concurrently open sheets, realistically one modal sheet per interaction/window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each sheet owns an independent DisposableStore and promise. There is no shared queue, but modal UX and caller guards generally constrain this to one active sheet per interaction; the new lifecycle callbacks do not launch asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted or populated. Cold and repeated openings construct a fresh bounded DOM tree and fresh listeners, as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the shell implementation directly shows the array construction, listener ownership, disposal, animation timer, and caller promise resolution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Picker item/focus-target counts vary by caller, but the changed key path removes work and the two additional event subscriptions are constant per live sheet.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added subscriptions are lifecycle-bound and constant per sheet; the focus change reduces repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close or unregister an auxiliary window while a mobile sheet is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM.onWillUnregisterWindow or DOM.onDidUnregisterWindow synchronously reaches the added filtered one-shot listener, invokes the existing dismiss/close path, disposes the sheet/body resources, removes the overlay immediately because the owner window is closing, and resolves the pending sheet promise.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The global window event evaluates one filter per concurrently active sheet; only sheets owned by the closing window proceed. Realistic effective cardinality is one active modal sheet in that auxiliary window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lifecycle delivery is synchronous. Event.once and DisposableStore disposal prevent duplicate teardown when both will- and did-unregister signals can occur; no burst of subprocess or remote work is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Teardown behavior is identical for cold and repeated sheet instances, and each instance removes its subscriptions on close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the window emitters, one-shot filter, close implementation, and regression tests establish the path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of users closing auxiliary windows with an open sheet is uncertain, but the prior retained-resource mechanism and the new bounded cleanup path are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a performance improvement, not a finding: it closes a cleanup-lifecycle hole that could retain DOM, listeners, body resources, and an unresolved continuation. The fixing mechanism was recorded with report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Replace, close, or dispose the connection-diagnostics Accessible View provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating the provider stores one snapshot reference. Accessible View context replacement or close disposes the provider; the newly registered disposal callback clears the contribution's reference when it still points to that provider. Contribution shutdown also disposes the current provider.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: State is one provider and one diagnostics snapshot per contribution, not an accumulating collection. Disposal executes one identity check and callback.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider generations can overlap briefly during replacement, but identity checks prevent an older disposal from clearing the current generation. There is no parallel boundary work or shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stored snapshot acts as a single-entry interaction snapshot while the provider is active and is invalidated on close/disposal. There is no negative cache or cross-provider accumulation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider construction, Accessible View onHide disposal, contribution disposal, and the new callback are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Snapshot size scales with configured/discovered/connected hosts plus at most 100 activity records, but only one snapshot is retained and the diff shortens its lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The common provider class gains one small disposable closure per low-frequency Accessible View provider, while the changed consumer releases caller-owned snapshot state earlier.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copy connection diagnostics after Accessible View disposal or while a diagnostics sheet is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: With an active sheet, copy uses its existing snapshot. Otherwise it uses the active Accessible View snapshot or synchronously rebuilds diagnostics from local in-memory service state, then awaits one browser clipboard write. Snapshot generation iterates effective host addresses and up to 100 activity entries but explicitly performs no discovery/network request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the generated diagnostics text through the browser Clipboard API, with an existing DOM execCommand fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one clipboard write per copy invocation; there is no per-host boundary fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same scenario performed one clipboard write. The only change is whether an already-disposed Accessible View snapshot is reused or current local state is serialized first.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The copy command awaits the clipboard write before announcing success.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Local snapshot CPU/allocation is O(H + A), where H is the deduplicated union of discovered, cached, configured, connected, dismissed/suppressed, and visible host addresses, and A is capped at 100. Clipboard bytes scale with the resulting text. One user copy invokes one clipboard write.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The sheet's copy action has an existing per-button pending guard. Command-level copy concurrency is unchanged by the diff; there is no new fan-out, and snapshot work is synchronous before the single clipboard operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm behavior while a provider/sheet is active reuses its interaction snapshot. After provider disposal, the changed path intentionally misses that single-entry snapshot and rebuilds current local state; no network cache is bypassed and there is no negative caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: getSnapshot's complete implementation and the clipboard service path establish cardinality, locality, serialization, and the awaited boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host counts and clipboard latency vary, but activity is capped and snapshot generation uses only local cached/service state. The extra rebuild occurs only on a user copy after provider disposal.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff can add one bounded local O(H + A) snapshot rebuild to a post-disposal copy, but it does not add remote I/O or clipboard calls and is user-triggered rather than hot.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review across all changed files and relevant transitive lifecycle, rendering, snapshot, and clipboard paths. No actionable performance regression was introduced. The PR removes an auxiliary-window sheet cleanup leak and shortens diagnostics snapshot retention; the concrete sheet lifecycle regression fix was recorded internally.
